source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's OCB1 campus in Council Bluffs publishes 9 MW of IT capacity across 420,000 square feet, the largest published figure of Iowa's two documented facilities.

The published number is a nameplate for the building, not a description of its contents. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 9 MW supports roughly 225 racks; at 10 kW per rack, roughly 900. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no tenant list, so neither figure describes what is installed. The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, qualify the campus for regulated workloads. They do not establish that any particular tenant or training cluster is present.

Iowa holds 52 mapped facilities, but only two publish a megawatt figure, totaling 18 MW. OCB1 is half that published total and ranks first in the state by published capacity. The gap between 52 mapped sites and two published figures is the signal: most Iowa capacity is invisible in the public record. Published megawatts describe a small, documented slice of a much larger buildout, and any statewide total built from them understates what is actually being constructed.

What this does not tell the reader is how much power OCB1 actually draws, whether it serves AI workloads at all, or how the other 50 Iowa sites compare. The 9 MW is a published capacity figure from one operator's spec page, retrieved 2026-10-04, and nothing here measures utilization, expansion, or the grid connections behind it.
